text: 126 Velleda is a main-belt asteroid classified as an S-type, likely representative of a typical but sizable member of this group. It is named after Veleda, a priestess and prophet of the Germanic Bructeri tribe. The asteroid was discovered on 5 November 1872 in Paris, France, by Paul Henry, marking his first credited discovery. Together with his brother Prosper Henry, they discovered a total of 14 asteroids. 126 Velleda orbits the Sun with a period of 3.81 years and an orbital eccentricity of 0.11, and its orbital plane is inclined by 2.9° relative to the ecliptic plane. It has a cross-sectional diameter of approximately 45 km. The asteroid completes one rotation every 5.36 hours, and its brightness varies by 0.22 magnitudes during each rotation.
